findings.passage: “The integrity of the voter roll is paramount to the entire electoral process and we must restore confidence in the voter roll for future elections for all Texans,”
findings.note: Statement issued in his name when he and five joint authors filed seven election bills, including one on checking citizenship of registered voters.

findings.passage: Why do you believe that those who self-identify as non-citizens should remain on the voter roll?
findings.note: His letter answering a newspaper editorial about his seven election bills; it describes SB 1114 as requiring the Secretary of State to cross-reference voter rolls and motor vehicle records where a person indicated they are not a U.S. citizen, and to remove those voters.

findings.passage: SB1112 – prevents local election officials from suspending the requirement of the Early Voting Ballot Board to verify that the signature on the mail ballot application and the signature on the mail ballot are from the voter. (This is a fundamental voter integrity issue in the United States.)
findings.note: His description of a bill on signature checks for mail ballots.

findings.passage: The fact is that non-citizens simply cannot vote in our elections.
findings.note: Press release on his site, quoting him on a county tax assessor's position about removing non-citizens from voter rolls; the release says he filed SB 1230 in the 85th session and would refile it.

Author of SB 1230, relating to cancelling a voter's registration when the person acknowledges not being a citizen. The history shows it referred to Senate State Affairs on this date, and no later action. Date is the referral date, not the filing date.

Author of SB 1114, relating to verification of the citizenship status of certain registered voters. Filed with five joint authors; the date is the date of his press release announcing the filing. The bill history shows it placed on the House General State Calendar on 2021-05-25.

Listed among the Senate authors of SB 16, relating to requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote, with a limited federal ballot for voters who cannot supply the proof. Date he was added is not on the page.

findings.motion: Third reading and final passage of SJR 37 (28 yeas, 3 nays)
findings.note: Senate vote on SJR 37, a proposed constitutional amendment clarifying that a voter must be a United States citizen. He is listed among the yeas on the second-reading, suspension and third-reading roll calls of that day.
